summary: Goderich's 1847 stone tower, the first lighthouse on Canada's Lake Huron shore: keepers from 1847, 1913 storm wreckage on its beaches, and Town ownership since 2003.

lens.note: Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1909: a 4th order French lens replaced the catoptric light. The current lens is not described in these sources.

structures.type: square stone tower, almost square plan
structures.note: Coast Guard list gives 10.1 m; Lighthouse Friends says 'just twenty feet tall to its lantern room'. Heightened 1914; eight-sided iron lantern and concrete murette (designation report).
Replaced the mast and lantern of the back light (1905). Lighthouse Friends gives 1908.
Western end of the breakwater (Department report, fiscal 1910).

staffing.note: Last head keeper in the Lighthouse Friends list: Donald Bert MacAdam, 1985 to 1992. When resident keeping ended is not stated in these sources.

access.note: Town-owned lighthouse in a public park at 280 Cobourg Street. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Contract let for the tower, to be complete by 1 July 1846 (Lighthouse Friends).
Erected 1847 (designation report). Lighthouse Friends: severe gales damaged the lantern in November 1846, before the lighting apparatus was placed in 1847.
Lighting apparatus placed in the tower in 1847; Killaly found the light showing on his 1847 visit.
Bank-protection work below the tower, completed summer 1873 for $3,850.
Five panes of French plate glass in the lantern; ten flat-wick burners.
Back light (fixed red on a mast) put in operation 5 September 1905 after a breakwater was built outside the piers.
4th order French lens replaced the catoptric light at the main light (Department report, fiscal 1909). Lighthouse Friends: 1908.
Back range light's pole and lantern replaced by a three-section steel skeleton tower. Lighthouse Friends dates the tower to 1908.
Reinforced concrete gas-lighted beacon, 15 ft high, on the western end of the breakwater. Lighthouse Friends dates it to 1909.
Wexford, James Carruthers and Regina foundered in the storm of 9-10 November 1913; crews lost; wreckage and bodies came ashore at Goderich. Inquest followed.
Electric compressed-air diaphone fog alarm at the western end of the north breakwater; run by the life-saving station on the south pier.
Tower heightened; gallery railing and stone lantern deck replaced (designation report). Lighthouse Friends: raised five feet, new lantern room and concrete deck.
A park created around the tower (1941-42, designation report).
Flashing red light on a small skeletal tower at the outer end of the south breakwater; radiobeacon VBD established at Goderich.
Present concrete tower on the southern breakwater.
Lighthouse and surrounding land sold by the Crown to the Town of Goderich for one dollar, dated 29 August 2003.
By-law No. 97 of 2009, passed 13 October 2009, designating the lighthouse under Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
Tower stripped of paint, repointed with period mortar, new door and windows, repainted; public opening June 2010.

wrecks.outcome: Foundered on Lake Huron in the storm of 9-10 November 1913, with her crew lost. Wreckage and bodies wearing her life preservers came ashore at Goderich (Lighthouse Friends; Perth Amboy newspaper).
Foundered on Lake Huron in the same storm, crew lost. A Grand Forks wire dispatch from Goderich reported 'eight, men and one woman' bodies found on the shore.

Probably lost in the same storm. A Perth Amboy dispatch reports three bodies on a raft stamped with her name came ashore near Goderich, and later reports of twenty more. Single newspaper; not confirmed by a Department report.

notes_for_editor: Read: Lighthouse Friends (copyrighted; paraphrased, with short quotations only), the Ontario Heritage Trust copy of By-law No. 97 of 2009 with its designation report (OCR; the builder's name and the cost in pounds are not legible and are not used), the Canadian Coast Guard list (entry 777), Department of Marine reports in the corpus (fiscal 1905, 1909, 1910, 1911, 1914), and two Chronicling America pages from November 1913. Wikipedia and the Historical Marker database were not cited. Disagreements left open in the text: construction (contract for completion by 1 July 1846 and gales in November 1846 per Lighthouse Friends; erected 1847 per the designation report); tower height (10.1 m per the Coast Guard list; about 20 ft to the lantern room per Lighthouse Friends; the OCR of the designation report reads 6.1 m base to vane); keeper's dwelling (removed about 1914 per the designation report; sold, moved and torn down in 1985 per Lighthouse Friends). Also: the lens year (Department: fiscal 1909; Lighthouse Friends: 1908); the back light's steel tower (Department: fiscal 1909; Lighthouse Friends: 1908); Robert Campbell's end date (Lighthouse Friends: 1910; the Department's 1911 keeper list still shows him against Goderich Lights, read by position from the OCR). Lighthouse Friends gives the foghorn testimony with the date 'February 9', which conflicts with the Department's storm dates of 9 and 10 November 1913; the story does not give that date. The Carruthers 'eight men and one woman' figure is from one wire story and is attributed as reported. The McGean 'twenty more bodies' is a single later report and is marked unconfirmed. Killaly's 1847 words are read through Lighthouse Friends; his report is not in the corpus. The Huron Signal quotation is second-hand through Lighthouse Friends. The Thomas Mercer Jones sale to the Crown rests on Lighthouse Friends alone (a historical marker gives March 1849; not used). The post-1960 keepers (Comier, Sheardown, MacDonald, MacAdam) are named only as Lighthouse Friends prints them, with no personal detail. The Lighthouse Friends page for Goderich Breakwater (ID 1044) is a separate station and is not used. The keepers' appointment for Robert Campbell is by position in an OCR table. Staffing: the Lighthouse Friends list ends with keeper MacAdam (1985 to 1992); when keeping ended is not stated. Current lens not described in these sources. Record's 10.1 m and CCG figures agree. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Robert Campbell's appointment (9 June 1886) was read from the 1911 page image (scan 254), since the OCR gives only 'June'. The Campbell and Roque rows of the 1911 list, and the 1910 beacon row (scan 85: Goderich, contract to Wm. Bermingham), were confirmed on the page images. The 1909 back range tower (fiscal 1909; Lighthouse Friends 1908) and the 1910 beacon (fiscal 1910; Lighthouse Friends 1909) now carry the fiscal-year wording with both dates. Lighthouse Friends gives no separate restoration year; the story gives the 2009 approach and the June 2010 opening.
